title: Speculative commit arbitration with kernel-cost curation and soft rollback playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We need a low-latency, high-availability speculative decode flow that minimizes wasted cycles on expensive kernels while preserving output quality. Current optimistic decode flows accept candidate outputs aggressively which can waste high-cost kernel time or produce poor-quality responses when confidence signals are noisy. This ticket drafts a commit arbitration mechanism that gates speculative commits with a lightweight confidence signal, uses a kernel-cost curation step to prefer cheaper accept candidates early, and defines a soft rollback/fallback playbook when late signals indicate the optimistic branch is invalid.
background: Redwood's runtime supports multiple kernel variants (fp16/quantized/specialized attention kernels) and model variants. For short-latency requests we often run an optimistic lightweight decoder on a cheap kernel and in parallel run a higher-fidelity decoder on an expensive kernel. We need a systematic way to decide when the cheap branch's output can be committed versus when to wait for the expensive branch, and how to unroll or compensate when a late mismatch occurs.
design_goals: Minimize end-to-end latency for common short outputs while limiting wasted GPU time on expensive kernels
Provide measurable commitment confidence and diagnostic telemetry for post-hoc evaluation
Guarantee deterministic rollback behaviour and user-visible degradation strategies
Keep the API and routing configuration simple for product teams and compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments
proposed_design_summary: Introduce a commit-arbiter stage in the runtime scheduler. The arbiter receives candidate tokens/frames from multiple decoder tracks (cheap-fast and expensive-accurate). Each candidate is scored by: 1) commit-confidence (model-calibrated logit gap + n-gram stability), 2) kernel-cost-penalty (static kernel cost estimate + dynamic GPU load factor), and 3) coherency with cached prefix (KV-consistency penalty). The arbiter computes a composite commit score and applies a tiered threshold: immediate-commit for high scores, delayed-commit for medium scores (wait up to X ms or until expensive branch responds), and reject for low scores (allow expensive branch to commit). On late mismatch detection, the soft rollback plan uses a deterministic reconciliation: mark the optimistic output as provisional in internal trace, issue an on-the-wire correction event to client (streamed delta or replacement chunk), and increment per-request rejection counters for learning. A runtime switch allows conservative vs aggressive commit policy per route/tenant.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P50 latency improves by >=10% on conversational short-turn benchmark with aggressive policy compared to no-speculative baseline
Wasted expensive-kernel GPU time (allocated but unused due to optimistic commit) reduced vs naive speculative baseline by >=25% when kernel-cost penalty enabled
False-commit rate (cases where optimistic commit later conflicts with accurate branch) under aggressive policy stays <=0.5% for production prompts in telemetry sample
Soft rollback path implemented with client-visible correction event and associated unit/integration tests
Runtime feature flag + per-route config exists and documented in Console runtime settings
detailed_decisions: Signal composition: commit-confidence will combine logit-gap, token-stability across last 3 tokens, and a lightweight critic head score if available
Kernel-cost model: maintain a small table of relative kernel costs (e.g., cheap-quantized=1, fp16-optimized=2.4, attn-optimized=3.1) modulated by host-level load factor
Thresholding: use three thresholds (immediate, buffer, reject) tunable per release with rollback window default 150ms
Fallback: when expensive branch diverges, do not re-play entire stream; instead send minimal patch (replace last N tokens or append correction) to reduce client disruption
Telemetry: emit per-decision records with candidate scores, kernel chosen, latency to commit, and rollback reason to the Console ingestion pipeline
implementation_tasks: Runtime: Add commit-arbiter module in scheduler and event hooks for candidate producers
Model infra: add lightweight critic output to selected model variants and a training script to calibrate logit-gap to empirical acceptance
Kernel catalog: populate kernel-cost table and expose dynamic load factor from node agent
API: define correction event format for streaming clients and update SDK docs
Telemetry: add dedicated tables and dashboards for commit-decisions, false-commit rates, and wasted-kernel-time
E2E tests: unit tests for arbiter logic, integration tests with two-track decode emulation, chaos tests for late expensive branch arrival
safety_and_rollback_playbook: Feature-flagged rollout starting with internal tenants and low-QPS routes
Canary targets: 1% of production traffic -> 5% -> 25% with metric gating
Gates: false-commit rate, error spikes, increased token-cost per request
Soft rollback behaviour: if false-commit exceeds threshold, automatically disable immediate-commit policy and expand delayed window for the route
Operational runbook entry: steps to disable arbiter, collect diagnostic traces, and force-expensive-commit for impacted customers
telemetry_and_alerting: Logs: decision_record event with score breakdown and candidate hashes
Dashboards: per-route breakdown with histogram of commit scores and latency windows
Alerts: auto-trigger when false_commit_rate > 0.8% over 10m or wasted_expensive_ms increases by >50% vs baseline
test_plan: Synthetic bench: run dual-track decode over 100k short prompts to validate latency and false-commit rates
A/B: route 20% of beta customers to aggressive policy and compare end-user satisfaction metrics and token costs
Chaos: inject 200ms jitter to expensive branch to ensure arbiter respects buffer thresholds and falls back gracefully
Compatibility: verify streaming SDK handles correction events for JS, Python, and mobile SDKs
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal testbed + perf runs; iterate thresholds
Week 2: internal tenants + canary on low-QPS routes (1%)
Week 3: expand to 5% with telemetry gating; collect false-commit and cost savings reports
Week 4: 25% traffic with manual review; if gates green, flip default policy for short-turn conversational model routes
Post-rollout: 90-day monitoring window and automatic calibration job to adjust thresholds based on drift
notes: Spoke with UX about user-visible correction semantics; prefer replacement chunk over delete-and-rewrite to avoid broken streaming parsers
Model team recommended a tiny critic head; they estimate ~2% increase in encoder cost but large improvement in calibration
Diego to prototype arbiter scoring function in /sandbox by 2026-03-10
